```{r}
# =============================================================
# Curation Notes - PRJEB15057
# =============================================================
# project_id   : PRJEB15057
# sra_file     : SraRunTable.csv (Earth Microbiome Project via ENA)
# paper        : Piombino et al. (2014) "Saliva from Obese Individuals
#                Suppresses the Release of Aroma Compounds from Wine"
#                PLoS ONE 9(1): e85611. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0085611
#
# bioproject     : initial_meta column 'BioProject'
# sample_id      : initial_meta column 'Run'
# subject_id     : initial_meta column 'host_subject_id' (subject initials)
# age            : initial_meta column 'AGE' (numeric, unit=years)
# age_info       : Paper Table 1 — age ranges: O=21-68, N=20-60
# bmi            : NOT directly available as numeric; BMI class flags exist
#                  (bmi_185_249, bmi_30_349, etc.); marked NA
# sex            : initial_meta column 'sex' — all values "male" -> "M"
# sequencing_region : Paper Methods "16S rRNA V4 region" — also initial_meta
#                   column 'target_subfragment' = "V4"
# platform       : Paper Methods "Illumina HiSeq2000"; also initial_meta
#                  column 'instrument' = "Illumina HiSeq 2000"
# country        : initial_meta column 'COUNTRY' — all "Italy: GAZ" -> "Italy"
# site           : initial_meta column 'env_material' — all "saliva" (clean value, no prefix)
# site_group     : "oral" (saliva is an oral site)
# public_time    : initial_meta column 'ReleaseDate'
# pcr_primers    : Paper Methods "515F-806R"; also initial_meta
#                  column 'pcr_primers..exp.' = "FWD:GTGCCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA;
#                  REV:GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT"
# title          : Paper title
# disease_study  : "yes" — study compares obese vs normal-weight individuals
# status         : Derived from initial_meta column 'body_status'
#                  "normal" -> "HC", "obese" -> "obesity" (full name,
#                  not a standard abbreviation in the template list)
# matched_samples: "no" — each subject has one saliva sample (two collections
#                  pooled before analysis, per paper Methods)
# is_time_series : "no" — single timepoint design; paper Methods states
#                  "The collection was repeated twice and the samples were
#                  pooled per participant prior to further analyses"
#                  — not repeated measures over time
# controls       : none found in metadata or paper
# non-human      : initial_meta column 'Organism', keyword "human oral
#                  metagenome" — all samples are human, none removed
# =============================================================
```

# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

This step sets the project directory, loads the raw SRA metadata, and optionally merges supplement tables.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

# (1) Setting working directory
project_id <- "PRJEB15057"

base_dir <- "D:/metadata_collect"
setwd(file.path(base_dir, project_id))

# (2) Loading raw SRA metadata file
sra_file <- "SraRunTable.csv"
initial_meta <- read.csv(sra_file, header = TRUE)

# (3) No supplemental tables available for this project
```

# Step 3: Removing Control and Non-human Samples

First, we need to remove control samples(including both negative controls and positive controls) and non-human samples.

```{r}
# (1) Parameter setup
# From paper: no control samples mentioned; all 56 are human saliva donors
control_column <- ""   # no control column
control_keywords <- c()     # no controls in this study

species_column <- "Organism"          # column for organism identification
unique(initial_meta[[species_column]])
non_human_keywords <- c("Pet", "dog", "cat", "mouse", "rat", "environmental")  # none present; all human

# (2) Remove controls and non-human samples. DO NOT need to modify code in this part, just run it.
n_samples <- nrow(initial_meta)
# Control evaluation
if (length(control_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(control_column) || control_column == "") {
    stop("Error: control_keywords provided but control_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(control_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", control_column))
  }

  control_pattern <- paste(control_keywords, collapse = "|")
  control_text <- initial_meta[[control_column]]
  is_control <- grepl(control_pattern, control_text)

} else {
  is_control <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Non-human evaluation
if (length(non_human_keywords) > 0) {
  if (is.null(species_column) || species_column == "") {
    stop("Error: non_human_keywords provided but species_column is missing.")
  }

  if (!(species_column %in% colnames(initial_meta))) {
    stop(sprintf("Error: Column '%s' not found in initial_meta.", species_column))
  }

  non_human_pattern <- paste(non_human_keywords, collapse = "|")
  species_text <- initial_meta[[species_column]]
  is_non_human <- grepl(non_human_pattern, species_text)
} else {
  is_non_human <- rep(FALSE, n_samples)
}

# Execute removal
samples_to_remove <- is_control | is_non_human
initial_meta <- initial_meta[!samples_to_remove, ]

cat("Initial samples counts:",n_samples,"\n")
cat("Removed control samples:", sum(is_control), "\n")
cat("Removed non-human samples:", sum(is_non_human), "\n")
cat("Total samples removed ", sum(samples_to_remove), "\n")
cat("Remaining samples after Step 2:", nrow(initial_meta), "\n")
```

# Step 4: Creating a Uniform Metadata Template

This step converts the raw SRA table into the standard metadata format used in our meta-analysis.
The uniform metadata should include the following columns:
1. **bioproject**: Project ID from SRA or other database
2. **sample_id**: SRA sample/run ID. Unique id for each sample!
3. **subject_id**: subject id for each person if available.
4. **age**: Age of the subject if available.
5. **age_info**: If the age is not explicitly stated but approximate age range information is available, mark it in this column.
6. **bmi**: Body Mass Index if available.
7. **sex**: Sex of the subject. Mandatory to write as M/F.
8. **sequencing_region**: Targeted 16S rRNA region.
9. **platform**: Sequencing platform.
10. **country**: Country of sample origin.
11. **site**: Sampling site.
12. **site_group**: only accepts one of following three values: 'oral', 'gut', or 'other'.
13. **public_time**: Data release date.
14. **pcr_primers**: PCR primers used.
15. **title**: Title of the associated publication.
16. **disease_study**: Whether the study involves disease samples.
17. **status**: Disease status for each sample if available, else record as NA.
18. **matched_samples**: Whether the subject has matched samples.
19. **is_time_series**: Whether the study is a time series study.

```{r}
# Extract columns from initial_meta as follows:
# (1) No modification needed -> extract directly.
# (2) Modification needed -> create a new column with the prefix raw_ and mark the original column as "pending".
# (3) Need to find or determine based on the article.
metadata <- data.frame(
  bioproject = initial_meta$BioProject,
  # From initial_meta column 'Run' — unique run ID per sample
  sample_id = initial_meta$Run,
  # From initial_meta column 'host_subject_id' — subject initials
  subject_id = initial_meta$host_subject_id,
  # From initial_meta column 'AGE' (numeric, unit=years per 'age_unit' column)
  age = initial_meta$AGE,
  # From paper Table 1: O subjects age range 21-68, N subjects 20-60
  age_info = NA_character_,
  # BMI not available as numeric; only BMI class flags exist in CSV
  # (bmi_185_249, bmi_25_299, bmi_30_349, bmi_35_399, bmi_greater_40)
  # Cannot reconstruct exact BMI -> NA
  bmi = NA_real_,
  # From initial_meta column 'sex' — all values are "male"
  sex = "M",
  # From initial_meta column 'target_subfragment' — all "V4"
  # Also confirmed in paper Methods: "16S rRNA V4 region"
  sequencing_region = initial_meta$target_subfragment,
  # From paper Methods: "Illumina HiSeq2000"
  # Also matches initial_meta column 'instrument'
  platform = "Illumina HiSeq 2000",
  # From initial_meta column 'COUNTRY' — all "Italy: GAZ" -> "Italy"
  country = gsub(": GAZ", "", initial_meta$COUNTRY),
  # From initial_meta column 'env_material' — all "saliva"
  site = initial_meta$env_material,
  site_group = "pending",
  # From initial_meta column 'ReleaseDate'
  public_time = initial_meta$ReleaseDate,
  # From paper Methods: "515F-806R" (Earth Microbiome Project primers)
  # Also matches initial_meta column 'pcr_primers..exp.'
  pcr_primers = "515F-806R",
  # Paper title
  title = "Saliva from Obese Individuals Suppresses the Release of Aroma Compounds from Wine",
  # Paper studies obesity (obese vs normal-weight)
  disease_study = "yes",
  # From initial_meta column 'body_status': "normal" -> "HC", "obese" -> "obesity"
  raw_status = initial_meta$body_status,
  status = "pending",
  # Paper Methods: two collections pooled per participant, one final sample
  matched_samples = "no",
  # Single timepoint; no repeated sampling over time per individual
  is_time_series = "no",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
metadata$public_time <- as.Date(metadata$public_time)
```

# Step 5: Manually solving pending issues

This step involves two parts: (1) handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix, and next (2) handle the `site_group` and `matched_samples` columns.

```{r}
# (1) Handle the columns with the `raw_` prefix.

# Resolve status: map body_status to standardized values
# From initial_meta column 'body_status': "normal" -> "HC", "obese" -> "obesity"
# "obesity" is not in the standard abbreviation list (HC/CD/CRC/COPD/HIV/ICU/OSCC/RA/UC)
# so we use the full disease name per template rule
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(
    raw_status == "normal" ~ "HC",
    raw_status == "obese" ~ "obesity",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))
```

```{r}
# (2) Filling the 'site_group' and 'matched_samples' columns
# editing site_group
unique(metadata$site)
# EDIT HERE: add oral sites
Oral_site = c("saliva")
# EDIT HERE: add gut sites
Gut_site = c("feces")
# just run
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(site_group = case_when(
    site %in% Oral_site ~ "oral",
    site %in% Gut_site ~ "gut",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  ))

# editing matched_samples, just run.
metadata$matched_samples <- ifelse(
  ave(metadata$subject_id, metadata$subject_id, FUN = length) > 1,
  "yes",
  "no"
)
```

```{r}
# (3) check if there is pending value in metadata. If there is pending value, go on modify the metadata.
# Function to check if a column contains "pending"
has_pending <- function(col) {
  if (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) {
    any(col == "pending", na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    FALSE
  }
}

# Check for any pending value
any_pending_value <- any(sapply(metadata, has_pending))

if (!any_pending_value) {
  message("Good! No cell contains the value 'pending'.")
} else {
  pending_cols <- names(metadata)[sapply(metadata, has_pending)]
  message("Columns containing 'pending': ", paste(pending_cols, collapse = ", "))
  message("Please continue to resolve these pending columns!")
}
```

# Step 6: Visualize the Metadata

This step makes a quick set of plots for checking the distribution of key metadata fields.

```{r}
# Select columns for visualization, just run
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-bioproject, -sample_id, -subject_id, -title)

create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  continuous_vars <- c("age", "bmi")

  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (col %in% continuous_vars && is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = TRUE) +
        labs(title = col, x = col, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }

  return(plots)
}

# Generate and arrange plots
plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p <- plot_grid(plots$age,
               plots$age_info,
               plots$bmi,
               plots$sex,
               plots$site,
               plots$site_group,
               plots$sequencing_region,
               plots$platform,
               plots$country,
               plots$pcr_primers,
               plots$status,
               plots$matched_samples,
               ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
# Insert Metadata_Summary.png into the current Rmd output

```

# Step 7: Sort and export the metadata

This step saves the cleaned metadata table as the final `metadata_v2.csv` file.

```{r}
# Reorder the data frame
fixed_cols <- c("bioproject", "sample_id", "subject_id", "age", "age_info",
                "bmi", "sex", "platform", "sequencing_region", "pcr_primers",
                "country", "site", "site_group", "disease_study", "status",
                "title", "public_time", "matched_samples", "is_time_series")
metadata <- metadata %>%
  select(all_of(fixed_cols), everything())

# save metadata
# head(metadata)
write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata_v2.csv", quote = TRUE)
```
